examples.text: Сде́лав оди́н и́ли два поворо́та, геро́й наш очути́лся наконе́ц пе́ред са́мым до́мом, кото́рый показа́лся тепе́рь ещё печа́льнее.
examples.roman: Sdélav odín íli dva povoróta, gerój naš očutílsja nakonéc péred sámym dómom, kotóryj pokazálsja tepérʹ ješčó pečálʹneje.
examples.english: After turning round two or three corners, our hero found himself at last in front of the house, which looked even gloomier at close quarters.
examples.translation: After turning round two or three corners, our hero found himself at last in front of the house, which looked even gloomier at close quarters.

examples.text: Дом име́л тот немно́го неве́рный вид, како́й быва́ет, когда́ там, внутри́, спят лю́ди.
examples.roman: Dom imél tot nemnógo nevérnyj vid, kakój byvájet, kogdá tam, vnutrí, spjat ljúdi.
examples.english: The house had that slightly uncertain look that can happen when there are people sleeping inside.
examples.translation: The house had that slightly uncertain look that can happen when there are people sleeping inside.

glosses: house, home (as part of a name of an establishment)
plot (in some street addresses: a group of buildings sharing the same street number)

etymology_text: Inherited from Old East Slavic домъ (domŭ, “house; home”), from Proto-Slavic *dȍmъ (“house; home”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *damús, from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm (“home; house”)

glosses: tea (in all senses: the drink, the plant, the dried leaves, or tea-drinking)
tip (small monetary gratuity for a service worker)
raw_glosses: (slang) tip (small monetary gratuity for a service worker)

etymology_text:
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چای (çay), from Chinese 茶 (chá).
The “tip” sense derives from the expression дава́ть на чай (davátʹ na čaj) / дать на чай (datʹ na čaj) (literally, “to give [some money] for tea”).

glosses: methinks, must be, may be, hopefully, probably
raw_glosses: (colloquial) methinks, must be, may be, hopefully, probably

etymology_text: Clipping of ча́ю (čáju), first-person singular present of ча́ять (čájatʹ).

glosses: second-person singular imperative imperfective of ча́ять (čájatʹ)

etymology_text: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

examples.text: — Вот, Ле́ночка, — сказа́ла тётя, — я ухожу́, а ты остава́йся до́ма и будь у́мницей.
examples.roman: — Vot, Lénočka, — skazála tjótja, — ja uxožú, a ty ostavájsja dóma i budʹ úmnicej.
examples.english: - So, Lenochka, - auntie said, - I am going but you stay at home and be a good girl.
examples.translation: - So, Lenochka, - auntie said, - I am going but you stay at home and be a good girl.

examples.text: И пришли Матерь и братья Его и, стоя вне дома, послали к Нему звать Его.
examples.roman: I prišli Materʹ i bratʹja Jevo i, stoja vne doma, poslali k Nemu zvatʹ Jevo.
examples.english: His mother and his brothers arrived. Standing outside they sent word to him and called him.
examples.translation: His mother and his brothers arrived. Standing outside they sent word to him and called him.

glosses: Moscow (a federal city, the capital of Russia)

examples.text: Москва́ просну́лась и завизжа́ла трамва́ями. … Ле́тнее со́лнце ликова́ло над полнокро́вной землёй, и взо́рам двух люде́й предста́ла но́вая Москва́ ― чуде́сный го́род могу́щественной культу́ры, упря́мого труда́ и у́много сча́стья.
examples.roman: Moskvá prosnúlasʹ i zavizžála tramvájami. … Létneje sólnce likoválo nad polnokróvnoj zemljój, i vzóram dvux ljudéj predstála nóvaja Moskvá ― čudésnyj górod mogúščestvennoj kulʹtúry, uprjámovo trudá i úmnovo sčástʹja.
examples.english: Moscow awakened and screamed with trams. … The summer sun rejoiced over the full-blooded land, and two men appeared before the gaze of a new Moscow ― a wonderful city of powerful culture, stubborn labor and intelligent happiness.
examples.translation: Moscow awakened and screamed with trams. … The summer sun rejoiced over the full-blooded land, and two men appeared before the gaze of a new Moscow ― a wonderful city of powerful culture, stubborn labor and intelligent happiness.

examples.text: Москва́ впада́ет в Оку́ у го́рода Коло́мна.
examples.roman: Moskvá vpadájet v Okú u góroda Kolómna.
examples.english: The Moskva flows into the Oka River near the town of Kolomna.
examples.translation: The Moskva flows into the Oka River near the town of Kolomna.

glosses: the government of the Russian Federation
raw_glosses: (metonymic) the government of the Russian Federation

examples.text: Москва́ так и не отве́тила на тре́бования Вашингто́на.
examples.roman: Moskvá tak i ne otvétila na trébovanija Vašingtóna.
examples.english: Moscow has never responded to Washington's demands.
examples.translation: Moscow has never responded to Washington's demands.

etymology_text: Inherited from Old East Slavic *Москꙑ (*Mosky), originally referring to the river, probably from Proto-Slavic *mosky of unknown origin. Perhaps related to Czech moskva (“raw bread”), Slovak mozga (“puddle”), Polish Mozgawa, and more distantly Lithuanian mazgóti (“to wash, rinse”), Sanskrit मज्ज॑ति (májjati, “to sink”), Latin mergō (“to dive”). Doublet of Моско́вия (Moskóvija).
